title: Register copy loop
statement: Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a Boolean-valued oracle on four indices and Boolean words, and let $x$ be a Boolean word. For a copy-loop site $k$ and register state $\mathrm{st}$, suppose every register is at most $B$, the scratch register $Z$ is zero, and the sum of the destination and source register values specified by $k$ is at most $B$. The machine reaches the exit for $k$ from phase $0$ at that site, with the destination register increased by the source register's original value, all other registers unchanged, and the result unset; every configuration before the final one satisfies the guard requiring valid instructions and registers at most $B$.

every register of $\mathrm{st}$ is at most $B$
the destination plus source register values specified by $k$ are at most $B$
replaced:
Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be an oracle assigning a Boolean answer to
each of four indices and each Boolean word, and let $x$ be a Boolean word. For a
copy-loop site $k$ and register state $\mathrm{st}$, assume every register is at most
$B$, the scratch register $Z$ is zero, and the destination value plus the source value
specified by $k$ is at most $B$. Then the machine $A(E)$ can run from its initial phase
at site $k$ to the exit for $k$, replacing the destination register by the sum of its
original value and source value, leaving all other registers unchanged and the answer
unset; throughout the run, every intermediate configuration satisfies the guard
requiring valid machine instructions and all registers at most $B$.
